description: An introduction to the sciences of Hadith, covering the meaning of Hadith and Sunnah, the structure of a Hadith (sanad and matn), the classification of Hadith by number of narrators and reliability, the major collections and compilers, and the role of Hadith in explaining the Qur'an.

mcq.questionText: In Islamic studies, the term 'Hadith' refers to what?

options.text: The sayings, actions, and approvals reported from Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
The words revealed by Allah in the Qur'an
The Friday sermon given by an imam
The poetry of the Arabs before Islam

mcq.explanation: A Hadith is a report of what the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, did, or approved of, as transmitted by his companions.

options.text: Only the spoken words of the Prophet
The way, practice, and example of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
A book written by Imam al-Bukhari
The first chapter of the Qur'an

mcq.explanation: The Sunnah is the model way of life of the Prophet, including his words, deeds, and silent approvals, which Muslims follow as guidance.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Qur'an from the Hadith?

options.text: The Qur'an is the exact word of Allah, while Hadith is mainly the words and actions of the Prophet
Both the Qur'an and Hadith are recited in formal prayer (salah)
The Hadith was revealed first and the Qur'an came later
The Qur'an explains the Hadith and depends on it

mcq.explanation: The Qur'an is the literal speech of Allah revealed in Arabic, while the Hadith records the Prophet's own words and deeds; only the Qur'an is recited in salah.

mcq.questionText: A Hadith is made up of two main parts. What are they called?

options.text: The surah and the ayah
The sanad (chain of narrators) and the matn (text)
The fatwa and the ijma
The wahy and the tafsir

mcq.explanation: Every Hadith has a sanad (isnad), the chain of people who narrated it, and a matn, the actual content or text of the report.

mcq.questionText: What does the 'matn' of a Hadith refer to?

options.text: The chain of narrators
The actual text or content of the report
The name of the compiler
The number of times it was narrated

mcq.explanation: The matn is the body of the Hadith, the actual wording that conveys the Prophet's saying or describes his action.

mcq.questionText: A Hadith narrated by so many people at every stage that it is impossible they all agreed on a lie is called:

options.text: Ahad
Mutawatir
Mawdu'
Da'if

mcq.explanation: A mutawatir Hadith is reported by a large number of narrators in every link of the chain, giving certainty that it is authentic.

mcq.questionText: A Hadith reported by only one or a small number of narrators, not reaching the level of mutawatir, is known as:

options.text: Ahad
Mutawatir
Sahih only
Sunnah

mcq.explanation: An ahad Hadith is one transmitted by a limited number of narrators; it can still be authentic but does not reach the certainty of mutawatir.

mcq.questionText: Which classification describes a Hadith of the highest level of authenticity?

options.text: Da'if (weak)
Mawdu' (fabricated)
Sahih (authentic)
Hasan (good)

mcq.explanation: A sahih Hadith has an unbroken chain of trustworthy, accurate narrators and is free from hidden defects, making it the most reliable.

mcq.questionText: A Hadith that is reliable but slightly below the level of sahih, often because a narrator's memory was a little weaker, is called:

options.text: Hasan (good)
Mawdu' (fabricated)
Mutawatir
Sahih (authentic)

mcq.explanation: A hasan Hadith meets most conditions of authenticity but is slightly weaker than sahih; it is still acceptable as evidence.

options.text: A good but slightly weak report
A fabricated report falsely attributed to the Prophet
A report with a very large number of narrators
A verse of the Qur'an

mcq.explanation: A mawdu' Hadith is a lie invented and wrongly attributed to the Prophet; it is rejected and may not be used as proof.

mcq.questionText: Why is the isnad (chain of narrators) so important in the science of Hadith?

options.text: It makes the Hadith longer and more poetic
It allows scholars to check the reliability of each narrator and judge the Hadith's authenticity
It replaces the need to know the text of the Hadith
It is only used in the Qur'an, not in Hadith

mcq.explanation: The isnad lets scholars trace the report back to the Prophet and examine the honesty, memory, and connection of every narrator.

mcq.questionText: Who compiled the collection known as 'Sahih al-Bukhari'?

options.text: Imam Muslim
Imam al-Bukhari
Imam at-Tirmidhi
Imam Abu Dawud

mcq.explanation: Imam Muhammad al-Bukhari compiled Sahih al-Bukhari, regarded by Sunni Muslims as the most authentic book after the Qur'an.

mcq.questionText: The six famous canonical Hadith books in Sunni Islam are collectively known as:

options.text: The Kutub as-Sittah (the Six Books)
The Five Pillars
The Tafsir collections
The Books of Fiqh

mcq.explanation: The Kutub as-Sittah are the six major Sunni Hadith collections: the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) and the four Sunan works.

mcq.questionText: Which companion is famous for narrating a very large number of Hadith?

options.text: Abu Hurayrah
Imam al-Bukhari
Imam Muslim
Imam Malik

mcq.explanation: Abu Hurayrah is among the companions who narrated the greatest number of Hadith, having spent much time with the Prophet.

mcq.questionText: What is one of the main functions of the Hadith in relation to the Qur'an?

options.text: To replace the Qur'an entirely
To explain, detail, and clarify the teachings of the Qur'an
To cancel all the laws of the Qur'an
To translate the Qur'an into Swahili

mcq.explanation: The Hadith explains and gives practical detail to the Qur'an, such as showing how to perform prayer, which the Qur'an commands in general terms.

fib.questionText: The chain of narrators of a Hadith is called the sanad or _____.
fib.explanation: Sanad and isnad both refer to the chain of people who passed on the Hadith from one to another back to the Prophet.

fib.questionText: The actual text or content of a Hadith is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The matn is the wording of the report that conveys what the Prophet said or did.

fib.questionText: A Hadith narrated by so many people that they could not all have lied is classified as _____.
fib.explanation: Mutawatir reports reach the level of certainty because of the very large number of narrators at every stage.

fib.questionText: A Hadith narrated by only one or a few narrators is classified as _____.
fib.explanation: An ahad Hadith is transmitted through a limited number of narrators and does not reach the level of mutawatir.

fib.questionText: A Hadith of the highest authenticity, with a sound chain of trustworthy narrators, is called _____.
fib.explanation: A sahih Hadith has an unbroken chain of reliable, accurate narrators and no hidden defects.

fib.questionText: A weak Hadith that fails to meet the conditions of authenticity is called _____.
fib.explanation: A da'if (weak) Hadith has a defect such as a broken chain or an unreliable narrator.

fib.questionText: A fabricated Hadith falsely attributed to the Prophet is called _____.
fib.explanation: A mawdu' Hadith is invented and is rejected as a lie against the Prophet.

fib.questionText: The collection regarded as the most authentic book after the Qur'an was compiled by Imam _____.
fib.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari, compiled by Imam al-Bukhari, is considered the most authentic Hadith collection in Sunni Islam.

fib.questionText: The six major Sunni Hadith collections are together known as the Kutub as-_____.
fib.explanation: Kutub as-Sittah means 'the Six Books', the most respected Sunni Hadith collections.

fib.questionText: The wife of the Prophet famous for narrating many Hadith about his family life and teachings was _____.
fib.explanation: Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated many Hadith, especially about the Prophet's personal conduct and home life.

tf.questionText: The Qur'an and the Hadith are exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an is the literal word of Allah, while the Hadith is the record of the Prophet's words and actions; they are different sources.

tf.questionText: Every Hadith has two parts: the sanad (chain of narrators) and the matn (text).
tf.explanation: Scholars examine both the sanad and the matn when studying and grading a Hadith.

tf.questionText: A mutawatir Hadith is one narrated by only a single person.
tf.explanation: A mutawatir Hadith is narrated by a very large number of people at every stage; a report by one person is ahad.

tf.questionText: A sahih Hadith is more reliable than a da'if Hadith.
tf.explanation: Sahih means authentic with a sound chain, while da'if means weak; therefore sahih is stronger evidence.

tf.questionText: A mawdu' Hadith may be used as strong proof in Islamic law.
tf.explanation: A mawdu' Hadith is fabricated and is rejected; it cannot be used as evidence.

tf.questionText: Studying the isnad helps scholars decide whether a Hadith is authentic.
tf.explanation: By examining each narrator in the isnad, scholars judge the trustworthiness and accuracy of the report.

tf.questionText: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are two of the most respected Hadith collections in Sunni Islam.
tf.explanation: Together known as the two Sahihs, these collections are the most highly regarded after the Qur'an.

tf.questionText: Abu Hurayrah was one of the companions who narrated many Hadith.
tf.explanation: Abu Hurayrah is famous for narrating a very large number of Hadith from the Prophet.

tf.questionText: One role of the Hadith is to explain and give detail to the general commands of the Qur'an.
tf.explanation: For example, the Qur'an commands prayer, and the Hadith shows in detail how the Prophet performed it.

tf.questionText: Scholars accepted any Hadith without checking the honesty and memory of its narrators.
tf.explanation: Hadith scholars carefully studied the character, honesty, and memory of every narrator before accepting a report.

summary.correctAnswer: A Hadith is a report of the sayings, actions, or approvals of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
summary.explanation: Hadith records the words and deeds of the Prophet as preserved and passed on by his companions.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between the Sunnah and the Hadith.
summary.correctAnswer: The Sunnah is the way and example of the Prophet, while the Hadith is the recorded report that tells us about that example.
summary.explanation: Sunnah is the practice itself; Hadith is the written or transmitted account that informs us of the Sunnah.

summary.questionText: State the two main parts of a Hadith and what each means.
summary.correctAnswer: The sanad (isnad) is the chain of narrators, and the matn is the actual text or content of the Hadith.
summary.explanation: Both parts are examined by scholars when grading a Hadith.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between a mutawatir Hadith and an ahad Hadith.
summary.correctAnswer: A mutawatir Hadith is narrated by a very large number of people at every stage, giving certainty, while an ahad Hadith is narrated by one or a few narrators.
summary.explanation: The number of narrators in the chain is the basis for this classification.

summary.questionText: List the four common levels of Hadith based on reliability.
summary.explanation: These grades show how strong a Hadith is as evidence, from the strongest (sahih) to the rejected (mawdu').

summary.questionText: Why is the isnad considered important in the sciences of Hadith?
summary.correctAnswer: The isnad allows scholars to trace a Hadith back to the Prophet and to check the honesty, memory, and connection of each narrator to judge its authenticity.
summary.explanation: Without a sound isnad, the reliability of a report cannot be confirmed.

summary.questionText: Name two of the most famous authentic Hadith collections in Sunni Islam.
summary.explanation: These two collections, known as the two Sahihs, are the most respected after the Qur'an.

summary.correctAnswer: The Kutub as-Sittah are the six major Sunni Hadith collections: the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) and the four Sunan books.
summary.explanation: These six books are the most relied-upon Hadith sources in Sunni Islam.

summary.questionText: Describe two ways Hadith scholars verified the reliability of a Hadith.
summary.correctAnswer: They studied the character, honesty, and memory of each narrator, and they checked that the chain of narrators was unbroken and connected back to the Prophet.
summary.explanation: They also compared the matn with the Qur'an and other reliable reports to detect errors or contradictions.

summary.questionText: Explain one important function of the Hadith in Islamic law and life.
summary.correctAnswer: The Hadith explains and gives detail to the general teachings of the Qur'an, such as showing how to perform prayer, fasting, and zakat in practice.
summary.explanation: The Hadith is a primary source of Islamic law alongside the Qur'an and guides Muslims in applying its commands.

hoq.questionText: A student finds a saying attributed to the Prophet whose chain of narrators includes a person known by scholars to be a liar. According to the sciences of Hadith, how should this report be treated?

options.text: Accepted as sahih because it is about the Prophet
Rejected, because a narrator who is a liar makes the report unreliable, possibly fabricated (mawdu')
Treated as part of the Qur'an
Automatically counted as mutawatir

hoq.explanation: Because the authenticity of a Hadith depends on every narrator being trustworthy, a known liar in the chain causes the report to be rejected as weak or fabricated.

hoq.questionText: The Qur'an commands Muslims to 'establish prayer' but does not give every detail of how to pray. How does the science of Hadith help solve this for a believer?

options.text: It tells believers to ignore the command until it is clearer
It cancels the command of prayer found in the Qur'an
The Hadith records how the Prophet actually prayed, giving the practical details that explain the Qur'anic command
It replaces prayer with another act of worship

hoq.explanation: One main function of the Hadith is to explain and detail the Qur'an; the Prophet's recorded practice shows believers exactly how to perform the prayer the Qur'an commands.

hoq.questionText: Two reports describe the same event. One is reported by many narrators at every link of the chain; the other is reported by a single narrator. Which is more certain to be authentically transmitted, and why?

options.text: The single-narrator (ahad) report, because fewer people means fewer mistakes
The widely reported (mutawatir) one, because so many independent narrators could not all have agreed on a lie
Neither, because the number of narrators does not matter
Both are equal because they describe the same event

hoq.explanation: A mutawatir report has so many narrators at every stage that error or collusion is impossible, giving greater certainty than an ahad report by a single narrator.
